nodes.name: Hydrothermal MoS2 nanosheet growth
nodes.procedure: MoS2 nanosheets were grown on carbon cloths by a hydrothermal method with ammonium molybdate tetrahydrate [(NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O] and thiourea (CH4N2S) as the precursors.
nodes.source_text: Methods: MoS2 nanosheets were grown on carbon cloths by a hydrothermal method with ammonium molybdate tetrahydrate... and thiourea (CH4N2S) as the precursors.

nodes.name: NiFe LDH coating on MoS2
nodes.procedure: The obtained MoS2 nanosheets were immersed into a mixed solution of nickel acetate and ferrous sulfate to adsorb Fe and Ni ions onto the surface. After drying in air, the MoS2/NiFe LDH pre-catalysts were constructed. The ratio of Ni and Fe in the LDH can be easily controlled by varying the ion ratio in the solution.

nodes.source_text: Results: The obtained MoS2 nanosheets were immersed into a mixed solution... After drying in air, we obtained a hetero-structured pre-catalyst... The ratio of Ni and Fe in the LDH can be easily controlled...

nodes.name: Electrochemical activation
nodes.procedure: The MoS2/NiFe LDH pre-catalysts were subjected to cyclic voltammetry activation in 1 M KOH solution to obtain self-reconstruction Mo doping NiFe (oxy)hydroxide through Mo leaching.
nodes.source_text: The MoS2/NiFe LDH pre-catalysts were subjected to cyclic voltammetry activation in 1 M KOH solution to obtain self-reconstruction Mo doping NiFe (oxy)hydroxide through Mo leaching.

nodes.name: NiFe oxyhydroxide reference synthesis
nodes.procedure: The NiFe (oxy)hydroxide reference sample was synthesized by a commonly used wet-chemical method. Further detailed information about NiFe and MoNiFe (oxy)hydroxides synthesis can be found in Supplementary note 9, 10.
nodes.source_text: The NiFe (oxy)hydroxide reference sample was synthesized by a commonly used wet-chemical method.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows that the (oxy)hydroxide layer uniformly covers the carbon fiber.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Fig. 1c) shows that the (oxy)hydroxide layer uniformly covers the carbon fiber.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM results show ultrathin MoNiFe (oxy)hydroxide flakes with atomic thickness of 0.8 nm (monolayer) or 1.5 nm (double-layer).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic force microscopy (AFM) results of the (oxy)hydroxide flake prepared by ultrasonic treatment suggest that the active catalyst was ultrathin with an atomic thickness of 0.8 nm (mono-layer, denoted as 1 L) or 1.5 nm (double-layer, denoted as 2 L) (Fig. 1d).

properties.data_description: Oscillating profile showing layered structure heights

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines Ni, Fe, and Mo contents of 48.7, 19.4, and 0.11 μg/cm² respectively, indicating 0.1% Mo doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Using inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES), the Ni, Fe, and Mo contents of the obtained catalyst were determined to be 48.7, 19.4, and 0.11 μg/cm², respectively, indicating a small concentration (0.1%) of Mo doping in MoNiFe-27% (oxy)hydroxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms the presence of Mo dopant in NiFe (oxy)hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of Mo dopant in NiFe (oxy)hydroxide was further confirmed by the aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscope (HAADF-STEM) (Supplementary Fig. 4).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.2 nm assigned to the (105) plane of oxyhydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spacing between two adjacent lattice planes is quantified to be 0.2 nm (Fig. 1f), which is assigned to the (105) plane of oxyhydroxide.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image with scale bars and annotations

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern exhibits diffraction rings of (101), (110) planes for Ni-based hydroxide and (105), (006) planes for Ni-based oxyhydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the (oxy)hydroxide in Fig. 1g exhibits clear diffraction rings of (101), (110) plane for Ni-based hydroxide (PDF-#14-0117) and (105), (006) plane for Ni-based oxyhydroxide (PDF-#06-0075).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructure with visible lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping reveals uniform distribution of O, Fe, Ni, and Mo elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping revealed the uniform distribution of O, Fe, Ni, and Mo elements in MoNiFe (oxy)hydroxide (Fig. 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge sXAS shows decreased intensity after Mo doping indicating weakened metal-oxygen hybridization; Ni/Fe L-edge show increased intensity suggesting higher metal oxidation states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 6a, the intensity of O K-edge decreases after Mo doping... the increased intensity of Ni L-edge and Fe L-edge peak for MoNiFe (oxy)hydroxide (Fig. 6b, c).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms higher metal oxidation state in MoNiFe (oxy)hydroxide and higher defective oxygen content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS analysis (Fig. 6d, Supplementary Fig. 33-34) provided the same conclusion of higher metal oxidation state in the MoNiFe (oxy)hydroxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ redox transition delayed after Mo doping; Ni³⁺-O peaks at 476 and 557 cm⁻¹ emerge at higher potential (0.48 V vs Hg/HgO) for MoNiFe vs 0.44 V for NiFe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two characteristic peaks of Ni³⁺-O were found on the Raman spectra at 476 and 557 cm⁻¹... The emergence of the Raman peaks of Ni³⁺-O occurred at 0.44 V and 0.48 V (vs. Hg/HgO) for NiFe and MoNiFe (oxy)hydroxide, respectively.
